summary: Add a board slice that owns cross-capability orchestration and board policy. Work-items and labels remain independent; the board depends only on their published server-side operation surfaces, never their persistence internals.

tree.purpose: Thin RSC route; obtains route params and renders the board view from the board read entrypoint.
Server-only read adapter; verifies the session, builds request context, invokes the declared board boundary, and maps failures to the RSC-facing result/navigation behavior.
Board orchestration: loads work items, removes archived items, batches label lookup, rejects inaccessible labels, groups by status, and returns the board projection.
Single application boundary declaration; validates input/output, normalizes typed failures, and reports once.
Board-specific types, status grouping shape, and pure projection rules.
Existing published work-item read operation; owns work-item persistence and visibility semantics.
Existing published label read operation; owns label persistence and actor visibility checks.
Existing work-item persistence modules; not imported by labels or boards.
Existing label persistence modules; not imported by work-items or boards.
Presentation component receiving the board projection as RSC props.

flows: GET/RSC render -> app/boards/[boardId]/page.tsx -> adapters/inbound/read/boards/load-board.ts -> verify server session -> use-cases/boards/entries/load-board.ts -> use-cases/boards/operations/load-board.ts.
Board operation -> work-items published read operation with board scope and actor context -> visible work items.
Board operation -> collect referenced label IDs -> labels published batch read operation with actor context -> visible label details or a typed forbidden result.
Board operation -> hide archived items -> attach returned label details -> group remaining items by status -> return BoardView.
Board read entrypoint maps not_found, forbidden, unauthorized, and unexpected failures to the RSC result; navigation decisions remain in the framework entrypoint, not in the boundary.

decisions.choice: The board slice owns composition and board-specific policy.
decisions.rationale: Combining two capabilities, filtering archived items, grouping by status, enriching labels, and rejecting inaccessible labels are not work-item or label persistence responsibilities.

decisions.choice: Board operations may call only the published operations/** surfaces of work-items and labels.
decisions.rationale: The capabilities remain independently changeable and do not import one another; board code cannot depend on their data modules or database clients.

decisions.choice: Use existing local capability APIs as typed operation surfaces; add a port only if either capability is remote-owned or must run independently of its current technology.
decisions.rationale: A local store defaults to a data module; a table-shaped repository port would add needless substitution.

decisions.choice: Re-verify the actor server-side at the board read boundary and pass request-scoped identity through every capability read.
decisions.rationale: RSC routing, hidden fields, and client validation are not authorization. Label visibility must be enforced by the label capability, with the board treating refusal as forbidden.

decisions.choice: Board loading is all-or-nothing when a referenced label is forbidden; return taxonomy-coded failures and never provider messages.
decisions.rationale: Silently omitting an unauthorized label could expose inconsistent policy. Boundary reporting occurs once; expected authorization failures are not exception telemetry.

decisions.choice: Use the RSC/request result as the initial cache owner; add shared or client caching only if a later requirement introduces polling, realtime, or shared client lifecycle.
decisions.rationale: This is a read-heavy server-rendered page with no stated client-cache requirement.

decisions.choice: Test board policy at the operation/boundary seam, capability filters against the real local store, authorization at the read adapter, and rendering at the UI layer.
decisions.rationale: Tests should assert observable outcomes and preserve the same seams used in production.

risks: If the existing work-item or label APIs expose only framework-bound entries rather than reusable server operations, introduce narrow internal operations in those slices instead of having the board call inbound adapters.
Batch label lookup must preserve the distinction between missing labels and forbidden labels; do not convert either into raw provider errors.
If board data is later cached, cache keys and invalidation must be scoped by board, tenant, and actor visibility.
